info.description:
End-to-end encrypted cloud storage API. All file content is encrypted on the client before upload; the server never sees plaintext. 

## Authentication
Include `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every protected endpoint. Tokens are obtained from `POST /auth/login` (30-day session) or `POST /tokens` (long-lived Personal Access Token).

post.description:
task 1512 (P1 security review on PR #87): `_not_impersonated:
NotImpersonated` — this endpoint mints a fresh `X-Confirm-Token`, same as
`confirm_opaque_*`/`confirm_passkey_*`. Without this guard an admin
impersonation session hits the OPAQUE-only session-freshness bypass below
(an impersonation session is always fresh by construction) and mints a
step-up token for the impersonated account with no password check at all.
Every step-up-minting endpoint refuses impersonation categorically — same
standard as `confirm_passkey_start`/`confirm_opaque_start`.

task 1512b (Codex P1 review on PR #90): `NotImpersonatedOrPat`, not plain
`NotImpersonated` — this endpoint was bare `auth: AuthUser` (no
`ConfirmedAction`) before task 1512, so a PAT-authenticated caller could
step up. Plain `NotImpersonated` looks up `sessions` only, so it
unconditionally 401s every PAT bearer — see that type's doc comment.

get.summary:
GET /api/v1/billing/credit-notes — list the caller's credit notes (task 0917).
Reads the local `credit_notes` table scoped to the authenticated user. Each
entry references its original invoice and carries the credited amounts (shown
negative on the client) + a relative `pdf_url`.

get.description:
Each entry carries the fields the web invoice list + PDF download link need:
number, date, period, the net/VAT/gross split, the treatment, and a relative
`pdf_url` (`/api/v1/billing/invoices/{id}/pdf`).
get.summary:
GET /api/v1/billing/invoices — list the caller's compliant Mollie invoices
(task 0916). Reads the local `invoices` table (the source of truth for the
EU-compliance documents) scoped to the authenticated user.

get.summary:
GET /api/v1/billing/profile — the caller's billing profile, or an empty shell
(`exists:false`, customer_type defaulting to `b2c`) when none has been saved.

put.summary:
PUT /api/v1/billing/profile — upsert the caller's billing profile. Validates
(typed 400 on failure), then UPSERTs (one row per user). `vat_validated` is
first reset to `'unchecked'` (so a changed/cleared number can never keep a
stale `'valid'`), then — for a B2B **cross-border** number — VIES (task 0914)
runs synchronously and flips it to `valid`/`invalid`/`invalid_format`/
`unreachable`. Per **D5** any non-`valid` outcome leaves the buyer on
destination VAT (the 0915 engine keys reverse-charge strictly on `'valid'`).
Returns 200 with the stored profile (including the resolved VIES state).

get.description:
Returns how much storage the authenticated user has consumed and their
current plan quota.  Trashed files count toward used_bytes.

```json
{ "used_bytes": 1234567, "quota_bytes": 5368709120, "percentage": 0.02, "trash_retention_days": 30 }
```

Place-of-supply resolution, in precedence order:
 1. explicit `?country=XX` (+ optional `?type=b2c|b2b`) query params — lets the
    form preview a country BEFORE the profile is saved (0919 flow);
 2. else the caller's saved `billing_profiles` row;
 3. else 400 `billing_profile_required` (no country to compute against).

Query params: `plan` (required, e.g. `basic`), `cycle` (`monthly`|`yearly`,
default `monthly`), `country` (optional ISO-2), `type` (optional `b2c`|`b2b`),
`quantity` (optional, for per-TB Business).

server-side at checkout and again at invoice time.

delete.description:
**Task 1921 (deletion-safety R3).** Only a row that is itself trashed is deleted, and a folder
only when its whole subtree is trashed:
- an item that is not in the trash: `409 not_trashed` (a mobile Trash-scoped confirmation
  keeps its earlier `403 confirmation_required`);
- a trashed folder that still holds a live row (one a pre-1914 write path, or a race, put
  there): `409 has_live_descendants` with the count, and nothing is deleted;
- the row and its subtree are locked `FOR UPDATE` in the same transaction as the `DELETE`, so
  nothing can be moved or written into the folder between the check and the delete.
